explain.say: At midnight on 14 to 15 August 1947, Jawaharlal Nehru told India's assembly that the nation was waking to life and freedom. Pakistan had become independent a day earlier. Yet the same weeks saw one of the largest and most violent migrations in history. Look at the timeline of the long road to freedom.

explain.say: Why two states? See the causes. From 1909 Britain created separate electorates by religion. In 1940 the Muslim League under Muhammad Ali Jinnah demanded Pakistan, and in 1946 it won most Muslim seats. A British plan for a loose united India failed, and in 1947 Lord Mountbatten brought independence forward by ten months. Which cause seems most avoidable?

draw.question: Why was British India partitioned?

because.label: 1946 elections
because.note: The League wins most Muslim seats.

because.label: Talks fail
because.note: 1946 plan for a loose union collapses.

draw.answer: Politics hardened, talks failed and Britain rushed out.

explain.say: Now the map. The provinces of Punjab in the west and Bengal in the east were cut in two by a line drawn by Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer who had never been to India before, in about five weeks. The line was published two days after independence. Families woke to find themselves on the wrong side. Imagine learning your new country from a newspaper.

Look at the sizes, all estimates: about 15 million people crossed the new borders, Hindus and Sikhs moving to India, Muslims to Pakistan. Between about 200,000 and 2 million were killed, and tens of thousands of women were abducted. Each number is a family. We remember them with respect. How might such memories shape the two countries today?

draw.text: Death estimates vary widely; historians still debate them.

explain.say: Now the historians. Older accounts blamed British divide and rule or Jinnah's separatism. Ayesha Jalal argued Jinnah used the Pakistan demand as a bargaining chip, while Urvashi Butalia and Yasmin Khan recovered ordinary people's experience. Thank you for thinking so carefully. Exam tip: combine high politics with local voices.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Many actors decided; ordinary people paid.

faq.a: Communal politics hardened after separate electorates were created in 1909; the Muslim League demanded Pakistan from 1940 and won most Muslim seats in 1946; the Cabinet Mission plan for a loose union failed; communal violence spread; and Britain, exhausted after the war, rushed its departure.

faq.q: How many people were displaced by Partition?
faq.a: About 15 million people, by common estimates, moved across the new borders in Punjab and Bengal. Estimates of deaths range from about 200,000 to 2 million, and tens of thousands of women were abducted.

Announced on 3 June 1947 by the last viceroy, Lord Mountbatten, it agreed to divide British India into India and Pakistan, partition Punjab and Bengal, and bring independence forward from June 1948 to August 1947.

The boundary drawn by the British lawyer Cyril Radcliffe, who had about five weeks and little local knowledge, to divide Punjab and Bengal. It was published on 17 August 1947, two days after independence.

Historians disagree. Older views blamed British divide and rule or the Muslim League's separatism. Ayesha Jalal argued Jinnah used the Pakistan demand to bargain for power in a united India and that Congress leaders accepted partition to secure a strong centre. Others stress local violence and fear.

facts: Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947 and India on 15 August 1947.
The Radcliffe Line was published on 17 August 1947.

quiz.say: When was the Radcliffe Line published?
quiz.why: It was made public on 17 August 1947, after the independence celebrations.

wrong.1: Radcliffe only arrived in India in July 1947.
